content_units: One-Evening AI Film Program for Older Teens

A strong four-film program should show how screen stories about artificial intelligence changed across time: optimism, fear, control, identity, and ethics. The selection below uses films from four different decades, stays away from NC-17-level content, and avoids extreme body horror while still giving a museum audience rich discussion material.
Option 1:   2001: A Space Odyssey (1968)     Landmark AI classic about human dependence on intelligent systems     149 min

-   Educational rationale:   This film is one of the most influential depictions of artificial intelligence in cinema, especially through HAL 9000 and the question of machine trust. It gives older teens a foundation for discussing how technology can appear rational, calm, and helpful while still becoming dangerous through conflicting instructions.
-   Key discussion themes:   human vs machine judgment; trust in automation; mission ethics; interface design and control; AI voice and personality
-   Audience sensitivity note:   Contains suspense, character deaths, and a slow, unsettling tone, but little graphic violence.
Option 2:   Blade Runner (1982)     Philosophical sci-fi about artificial beings and what counts as human     117 min

-   Educational rationale:   This film is excellent for examining personhood, empathy, memory, and whether artificial beings deserve moral consideration. It helps a teen audience move beyond “robots go bad” narratives into deeper questions about consciousness and social exclusion.
-   Key discussion themes:   personhood; memory and identity; empathy; creator responsibility; exploitation of engineered life
-   Audience sensitivity note:   Includes noir violence, some shootings, and a dark dystopian atmosphere.
Option 3:   The Matrix (1999)     Fast, accessible entry point into simulation, control, and digital reality     136 min

-   Educational rationale:   This film remains highly effective for introducing teens to questions about virtual reality, algorithmic control, and freedom inside machine-made systems. It also opens a useful conversation about how humans understand truth when their perceptions are shaped by powerful technological structures.
-   Key discussion themes:   simulation; control systems; reality vs perception; resistance; human energy and machine dependence
-   Audience sensitivity note:   Stylized action violence, gunplay, and intense sequences, but not extreme gore.
Option 4:   Her (2013)     Emotionally grounded story about AI companionship and human attachment     126 min

-   Educational rationale:   This film is especially useful for contemporary museum audiences because it shifts AI discussion toward relationships, loneliness, voice assistants, and emotional dependence on software. It gives older teens a relatable way to discuss whether connection with an artificial intelligence can be meaningful, ethical, or manipulative.
-   Key discussion themes:   AI companionship; loneliness; intimacy and ethics; emotional projection; limits of human-machine relationships
-   Audience sensitivity note:   Contains mature emotional themes and some sexual content in conversation, but minimal onscreen violence.
- It moves historically across changing AI ideas, from machine logic to artificial personhood to system-level control to emotional AI.
- It balances tone: philosophical opening, human-rights/identity middle, high-energy third slot, and a reflective closing film.
- If the museum plans introductions or short post-film discussions, this sequence creates a clear educational arc from “Can we trust AI?” to “What kind of relationship should humans have with AI?”
Program Fit for a Teen Museum Audience
Context note: A true one-evening event would be very long with all four films, totaling   528 minutes   of screen time, or   8 hours 48 minutes   before breaks and discussion.
-   Full marathon event:   best for a special late-day-to-night program with meal breaks.
-   Curated excerpt + discussion event:   show selected scenes from all four films plus one complete feature for a shorter evening education session.
